newsitem.title: USA: CVS to buy Revco for $2.8 billion.
newsitem.headline: CVS to buy Revco for $2.8 billion.

text.p: CVS Corp., the nation's fifth-largest chain of drug stores, said Friday it will acquire rival Revco D.S. Inc. for $2.8 billion in stock, creating the nation's second-largest drug store chain.

The combined company will have about 4,000 stores and annual sales of $13 billion, CVS said, making it the nation's largest in terms of outlets and second-largest behind Walgreen Co. in terms of total sales.
CVS stores are located primarily in the Northeast and Middle Atlantic regions. Revco stores are mostly in Midwest and Southeast.
The merger calls for CVS to pay the equivalent of $40.64 in its shares for each share of Revco, based on Thursday's closing stock prices. CVS also will assume $900 million of Revco debt.
CVS stock closed Thursday at $44 a share and Revco at $38, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
Both companies acknowledged last month that they were discussing a combination of their businesses.

The new company will retain the name CVS, will be led by the existing senior management of CVS and retain the CVS headquarters in Rhode Island. Revco's headquarters in Twinsburg, Ohio, will be phased out.
CVS said the only layoffs it anticipates would be in connection with the phase-out of Revco's headquarters.
CVS said the new company plans to open or relocate 300 stores a year after the merger is completed.
The merger follows Revco's acquisition in October of the Big B Inc. chain of 400 drug stores for $380 million.
Revco itself shook off a takeover attempt launched in November 1995 by Rite Aid Corp., which bid $1.8 billion for Revco.
